correctness.rationale: For a maximal corona packing, its core is a 2-packing S, and every private leaf not within the closed core neighborhood N_H[S] must be selected because it could otherwise be added. Conversely this exactly constructed set blocks every absent vertex, so there is a bijection. Disjoint closed neighborhoods of S give |N_H[S]|=|S|+sum deg_H(s), proving |P_S|=n-sum deg_H(s). The maximum, minimum, maximum-count, regular spectrum, complete-graph gap and cyclic-gap binomial formula follow by exact arguments. Direct subset enumeration of 1,249 core graphs with 10,647 corona maximal supports plus complete-base checks reproduced these identities. Finite tests are supplementary rather than a general proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a canonical representation and complete labelled cardinality enumerator for every maximal closed-neighborhood packing across an unrestricted graph operation. This is stronger than the maximum packing number and provides the exact lower packing problem as a degree-weighted 2-packing optimization on the base. It implies an arithmetic progression of sizes for all regular bases, a closed complete sunlet family enumerator, and arbitrarily large missing-size intervals in connected examples. Lower versus upper maximal-packing behavior is an active motivated problem, not an arbitrary finite census.
